vice-president of the commission. − mr president, i agree entirely with the members who have said that the high standards which we give to our citizens – rightly so – must also be transferred when there is an exchange of data with third countries. we in the commission take this question very seriously, because the commission believes and supports the principle that, in international public law, a legal act which is enacted by a third country cannot be directly and automatically applied in the territory of the eu unless – exceptionally – union law or member state law explicitly recognises the facts of such an act in their respective jurisdiction. no legal acts of a third country as such can legally overrule the relevant eu legislation or member state legislation, and this includes data protection rules. any processing of personal data in the eu has to respect the applicable eu data protection law. if – and this was mrs in ‘t veld’s basic question – a us law enforcement authority requires information from companies operating in the european union, whatever the nationality of those companies, they have to use existing channels of cooperation and mutual legal assistance agreements. this issue also applies when personal data are transferred by an eu company to a company in the us and when the data are subsequently processed for law enforcement purposes. this sounds good – except that this issue is not explicitly addressed in the current eu legal framework. that is exactly the reason why (as the rapporteur knows perfectly well) we have the data protection regulation, which the commission put on the table on 25 january to try to provide additional legal clarity in these matters. the regulation makes it clear that transmissions can only take place when the conditions of the regulation for such transfers are met, notably when there is a justification on an important ground of public interest – and the public interest has to be recognised in union law or in member state law. this could involve, for instance, data transfer between competition authorities, tax and customs administrations, and it could also be for the prevention and investigation, detection and prosecution of criminal offences. as you rightly said, this issue has been raised in the umbrella agreement on the protection of personal data. as parliament has been informed, this negotiation is still continuing. for the moment we have not yet reached a conclusion with this negotiation. as parliament also underlined, this is an element which, for my colleague who is responsible for taxation, has to be seen in the framework of the fatca regulations. here i would like to make it very clear (this may be new information for parliament) that the commission has raised this issue with the united states regularly and intensively in the framework of the financial markets regulatory dialogue and, as a result of the discussion, on 6 february the us announced that the foreign account tax compliance act (fatca) should be complied with by the transfer of data between tax administrations rather than by the imposition of direct obligations on eu financial intermediaries. so that is good news, which now has to be put into a clear text. but this is the direction we want to go in, and the commission will continue to work with the us and with the member states in order to identify the best way to address this issue and achieve legal certainty and compliance with the eu charter of fundamental rights. when i speak here about the united states, this means that it also applies to other third countries. the relations between the eu and the united states are those which are most discussed, but in future we will certainly also have many discussions about other continents with which we have a specific relationship.
on behalf of the ppe group mr president, i understand that data protection legislation can be based on internal security strategies. but we must not forget that its extraterritorial impact may infringe the rights of european citizens. more than doubts have arisen in the medicare act, fisa, patriot act or fatca cases. in many of them we find the obligation imposed on european financial institutions, understood in its broadest sense, to provide information of all kinds such as the ownership and nature of their accounts or the withholding of payments, among others. there is no prior resolution to justify the collection of all this data, nor do users know where it is going or for how long it will be stored. it is therefore necessary to take measures and to design a body of rules and legislation to avoid the violation of the principle of territoriality. we must be able to maintain the union's external relations and the security of our territory intact, but all this in full respect for the rights of all european citizens. the european commission must do this with much greater commitment and interest.

the next item is the joint debate on - the recommendation of emilio menéndez del valle, on behalf of the committee on international trade, on the draft council decision on the conclusion of the regional convention on pan-euro-mediterranean preferential rules of origin (11343/2010 - c7-0207/2011 - 2010/0093 ((nle)) (a7-0026/2012), and - the oral question to the commission on the proposal for a council decision on the conclusion of the regional convention on pan-euro-mediterranean preferential rules of origin, by emilio menéndez del valle and vital moreira, on behalf of the committee on international trade (o-000024/2012 - b7-0036/2012).
the european union must make it a priority to consolidate a single shore of peace, development, justice and freedom in the mediterranean. in the framework of the barcelona process, the association agreements with our mediterranean partners were the first step towards creating a euro-mediterranean free trade area. one of the main reasons why this target could not be reached in 2010 was the lack of social, economic and commercial integration between our neighbours to the south. the arab spring, as you know, represents the most momentous change since the fall of the berlin wall. in this context, the high representative and the commissioner for enlargement and european neighbourhood policy should be congratulated for giving priority to the convention, on which we are taking a decision today, as one of the commitments that make up the european response to this situation. this convention on pan-euro-mediterranean rules of origin is an important step towards the creation of the free trade area. its adoption will ratify a single, simplified instrument replacing the more than 100 existing bilateral protocols and extend its geographical scope to include the western balkans and efta, in addition to the mediterranean countries. the convention thus provides an incentive for south-south trade, which can contribute to economic growth and diversification, poverty reduction, democratisation and integration in the region. i hope that the commission will be able to answer in this debate the questions and concerns which parliament has almost unanimously put to us in the form of an oral question and a resolution. on the other hand, in addition to the absence of a dispute settlement mechanism, a review clause and an impact assessment, it is important to address the import and potential accumulation of origin of products originating, albeit redundantly, from illegal israeli settlements. i regret to add that although the current technical agreement between israel and the european union requires that israeli customs authorities and exporters examine whether or not products exported to the union originate in the colonies, the procedure does not provide for this distinction to be notified to european customs. this prevents our customs, which cannot check every consignment from israel in the absence of an extraordinary budget for this purpose, from being able to comply easily and effectively with international law and with their obligation to refuse the application of the preferential treatment of the eu-israel agreement to products originating in the territories occupied by israel. i therefore think that a commitment by the commission to a more appropriate, simple and effective approach to the determination of the real origin of products exported by israel which takes up the proposals in the resolution would be welcome and would ensure broad support for the convention, avoiding that this issue could hinder its adoption and the social and economic integration of the mediterranean region, which is so important, especially in the circumstances we are currently experiencing, for the european union as a whole.

president of the commission. mr president, let us give concrete answers to the questions asked. first, a question on the letter from the twelve governments. i said at the european council meeting that i could subscribe to practically every word of that letter. these were all very important elements for growth, including the deepening of the internal market and structural reforms. but i also reminded the member states of two aspects which i thought were important. first, there is no reference in this letter to the social dimension and the need to fight poverty. i believe that we need to combine some structural reform measures with proactive measures in social terms. secondly, i expressed my surprise at the european council that there was not a single reference to the europe 2020 strategy. this means that a strategy which has been unanimously approved by the european council is not even mentioned by the heads of state or government. council of europe. - mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i would first like to thank all those who have congratulated me on my re-election. i noticed that the enthusiasm was not the same in all the benches but i would say it's an old saying "to enthusiasm, no one is bound". there has been a lot of criticism of the general approach, but our general strategy, the one we have followed, both at the level of the union and at the level of the member states, is a strategy that has been supported by all the member states, by all the prime ministers and heads of state since the beginning of the crisis two and a half years ago, including in a different composition since among those who elected me two and a half years ago, there are still twelve. the current composition of the european council supports this strategy. at the last council, all 27 member states signed the tax compact. we can criticise the general approach, but i simply say that for the past two and a half years this strategy has been the unanimous strategy of the european council. of course, everyone is aware that this is a difficult, unpopular path, that it produces results only in the medium and, in some cases, even the long term. but this is the path we have chosen and we will remain consistent with it. in my introduction, i said in a very cautious way: our strategy is going to work. we have reached a turning point. normally, i am very careful, i was very careful in this case as well. and that was translated into saying that i would have declared that this was the end of the crisis, and so on. no, not at all. don't be afraid, i said this was the turning point of a very serious crisis. in the press, which is totally opposed to the european project and the euro project, there is no longer any talk of the end of the euro zone. it's pretty significant, but we don't talk about it anymore. are all the problems solved? no, of course not. but when i see that the interbank market is picking up after months of stagnation, that there is a significant drop in interest rates in a number of countries that were under pressure, we can say, indeed, that we have reached the bottom of the wave. but there is still a long way to go. the surest way to have positive economic growth like we had in 2010 and 2011, and which we lack in 2012, is of course to restore confidence in the future of the euro area. that's the very first condition for growth. what is missing in a number of countries now is that consumer and investor confidence in the future of the euro area. with the first signs of a return to growth in the euro, consumers and investors can follow. we are told that structural reforms are needed. i thought that there would be reference to structural reforms in the member states. no, we're talking about firewalls, we're talking about other initiatives in the financial sphere. but we forget that outside the firewalls - i think we will be taking decisions in the coming weeks - what is sustainable - of course, too little has been said about it - is structural reforms in the labour market and in the product market. restoring the competitiveness of both the member states and the union in general is what we need. if not, this crisis will come again. what really surprised me here was that the term 'european semester' was not mentioned even once. some have hinted at it, but hardly. the european council's aim was precisely to assess the european semester, to see where we are in terms of budget, macroeconomic and employment. member states are asked to present their reform plan and stability plan in the coming weeks. in may the commission will make recommendations. we shall discuss this again at the june council. if we do not take the european semester seriously, the crisis will one day return. i am disappointed that i have not heard much about this vital project which was approved by the european parliament and which was adopted with great enthusiasm over time. the long-term policy must be maintained - and this is the great challenge in a period of inevitable fiscal consolidation in virtually all countries. the president of the commission rightly referred to the europe 2020 strategy, and the whole point of fiscal consolidation is to set priorities, to consolidate and generally to reduce deficits and debt levels while safeguarding the future, by preserving a certain type of expenditure on research and development, education, training of young people, investments, particularly climate investments. the main challenge is to establish priorities in the midst of budgetary consolidation. of course, outside of that, there's fairness. that's why we've asked the banks for a huge contribution. they lose 70% of the present value of greek debt as contributions to the recovery of the greek situation. i agree with all those who have called for even stronger measures against tax fraud and evasion. the commission has just reiterated the measures it has taken. there is, of course, this rule of unanimity when it comes to taxation but there is a lot that can be done at national level. we do not always need the european framework. if there is a problem in greece, it is the problem of tax collection. this is the greatest injustice and the very source of the gigantic public deficit that it has. solidarity must of course be maintained in the midst of the policy of fiscal consolidation. that is why, at the level of the european union, we have provided aid to greece which is equivalent to 100% of greek gdp. if we want to have even stronger proof of the european union's solidarity with countries in difficulty, this figure is quite telling. we must keep the focus on climate objectives in the midst of fiscal consolidation. two are in the track. we still have to work on another one on energy efficiency. we again call on the member states to pursue a specific employment policy, in addition to fiscal consolidation. that is why we are looking forward to their employment plans for the month of april. we will assess them and this will be incorporated in the recommendations we will make to the member states in june. we need a specific policy for greece, we're working on it. the greek prime minister is fully committed to this. the deepening of the single market costs nothing in budgetary terms. there's the letter from the twelve. i do not agree with those who say that the letter of the twelve has not been taken into account. quite the opposite. in fact, after careful reading of the last draft conclusion, including on the single market, which i submitted to the european council, there was hardly any discussion, so much as the consensus elements of the letter from the twelve had already been taken into account. is there still room for further stimulus? i heard some words spoken. but the days of creating a policy of stimulus through public spending as in the past are over. it takes a much finer and much more sophisticated approach. we cannot avoid the policy of fiscal consolidation, but within this policy we must - as i said - keep a certain number of expenditure which is conducive to growth and employment under control. one last word on syria in bosnia. we can go much further with syria, on one condition: that we get a mandate from the united nations security council. it is not europe, it is not the european countries that are in the way, it is the two countries that are also named in the decisions of the european council that are a further step in the actions that we can take in relation to syria. it's not ours. we must also be aware that the united nations has a mandate to protect the people who are receiving humanitarian aid. we had a mandate for libya, we have used it fully - in other circumstances and for other purposes - but we have no mandate for syria. as far as bosnia is concerned, i had a very interesting interview with the new prime minister of bosnia and herzegovina. the european union is not a party to the treaty of rome, but it is a party to the treaty of rome. the european institutions and the european union are prepared to play their part as soon as possible, so that the european perspective can be maintained. it is for the first time that we will see the real european presence in that country which played such a tragic role in the civil war on the borders of the european union. here are some comments after the debate. i thank all those who have spoken.

in writing. − in december 2002, the council authorised the council presidency, assisted by the european commission, to start negotiating a mutual legal assistance agreement with norway and iceland. on 17 december 2003, the council adopted the decision concerning the signing of the agreement between the european union and the republic of iceland and the kingdom of norway on the application of certain provisions of the convention of 29 may 2000 on mutual assistance in criminal matters between member states of the european union and the 2001 protocol thereto. the agreement was based on articles 24 and 38 of the treaty on the european union. internal national procedures for this agreement had not been formally concluded at the time of the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon. as a consequence, according to the new legal framework provided for by the lisbon treaty and notably by article 218 tfeu, the consent of the european parliament is now required. in view of this, with the proposal for a council decision of 17th december.2009, the european commission has recommended to the council to obtain the consent of the european parliament and adopt a decision concluding the agreement without further delay.

in writing. - the situation of women in the union has stagnated in some respects and worsened in others in recent years. the economic crisis has negatively affected the position of women in the socioeconomic sphere, as cuts in social services, wages and employment have affected women more than men. it is essential that gender equality is further promoted in the eu and that member states are asked to prioritise this issue in their economic strategies. that is why i voted in favour of this report. the report is right about women's representation in all types of enterprises. it is vital that overall data on the representation of women in the union are collected in order to study the measures implemented in the business sector of the member states with a view to increasing this representation. the introduction of quotas is an effective and still necessary instrument for increasing female representation, as it allows progress towards gender equality and to some extent alleviates the consequences of the economic crisis for women.
in writing. − the european union has been an important player in fighting for gender equality anti-discrimination. however in spite of the best efforts, gender equality in the eu is far from being achieved. legislation may have changed, but traditional gender roles, gender stereotyping and taboos remain an important obstacle to fundamental change. the economic independence of men and women is key to gender equality. the current economic crisis risks putting us back years, as it may ultimately hit women hard than men. so efforts to improve labour market participation, and access to positions of power such as company boards, need to stay high on the agenda. the gap between the position and status of women and men in some countries outside europe is often dramatic. women have fewer rights or no rights at all. the eu and its member states need to do much more to improve the situation of these women, starting with their health. it is not only sufficient funds that are needed, but also a radical change in mentality and tradition.
in writing. − women's participation in political activities related to decision-making is alarmingly low. i am voting for the report because it proposes to change the current situation by promoting gender parity in decision-making processes. to achieve this objective, political parties in europe must be directly involved, for example by introducing quota systems for lists of candidates and elections, or alternating between female and male candidates at the top of the lists. it also urges national parliaments and the european parliament to take concrete measures to promote gender parity. as for the commission's actions in this case, i consider them to be a great step forward. however, to ensure successful implementation of these actions, political parties wishing to campaign for greater participation of women in decision-making should be provided with resources to do so. given that next year will be dedicated to european citizens, it is a great opportunity to encourage and finance actions to defend the rights of women in the union.

vice-president of the commission. − i shall start with ash. the ash crisis had serious lessons for us to learn, and we have also reached serious conclusions. after the first eruption of ash from eyjafjallajökull in april 2010, the coordination and collaboration mechanism between member states and the european institutions was strengthened, ensuring that the next eruption in april 2011 had far fewer negative consequences. the most significant project to facilitate air transport will definitely be the single european sky project, which is still developing and which will have a very important role to play in the trans-european network and in connecting europe facility projects. these will all make air transport easier and prevent serious delays.

member of the commission. − i share you view that a country cannot develop competitiveness in the long run purely by holding wages down. wages also play an important role in terms of sustaining aggregate demand in the economy, and demand is also very important if we want economic growth. however, given how the single market and the single currency have developed in the european union, we now have to ensure that imbalances do not undermine the stability and the growth potential of the european economy as such. while it is true that the european commission has no competences as regards wage-related questions, we have to see how, in the broader framework of economic governance, wage-related questions – wage trends, wage-setting mechanisms – can play a role in terms of developing a more stable and more dynamic environment. that is why last year, in the economic semester, some of the country-specific recommendations also pointed to certain wage-setting mechanisms which may have a role in helping – or, if they malfunction, undermining –economic competitiveness, which is why we engaged in dialogue with the member states. but this was – and continues to be – a dialogue. the commission is not imposing certain solutions on the member states, but we would like to see a constructive approach, and an understanding of the importance of these methods, on the part of the member states also.

you must look carefully, mr de backer, at all the texts that we are presenting or publishing, together with our colleague mr tajani in particular, and that is in particular the single market act. you will find in each case this particular attention - sometimes new - to the role, to the investment capacity, to the administrative ease, to the simplification, to give european smes the best ecosystem. let me give you an example. in the case of measures of bank capital, since this is the subject you are referring to, the question of where to find financing - we were talking about liquidity. with mr tajani, we asked the european banking authority if we could not go further - more balanced, less stringent measures for banks when they are obliged to provide for prudential measures when lending to small and mediumsized enterprises. we will maintain this more favourable criterion for small and medium-sized enterprises in prudential measures. in addition to the instrument we have just presented for venture capital, which is of particular interest to small and mediumsized enterprises, we have presented a passport which is currently being discussed in parliament. i am working, in particular, within the framework of mifid on the idea of a european sme exchange or a network of european sme exchanges. we have simplified the reporting requirements for small and mediumsized enterprises in accounting matters when they are listed - i am talking about listed companies - with the simplified prospectus, we have reduced the transparency requirements. we have made it easier for small and mediumsized enterprises to access public procurement by drastically reducing the administrative requirements for participating in tenders and we have also, within the framework of the small business act, for which mr tajani is responsible, closely followed all the measures which should facilitate investment by and through small and mediumsized enterprises.

member of the commission. − mr president, i welcome in the name of the commission the position of parliament on the guidelines for 2013 and what is more i agree with the major points as presented by the rapporteur, giovanni la via. indeed, properly shaping the last budget of the multiannual perspective 2007-2013 is quite a challenge, as is shaping it in the context of overall consolidation of national finances. nowadays austerity and consolidation are not the only dimensions of the economic debate in europe. what is next and what is equally important is how to boost investment, how to boost employment opportunities, especially for the younger generation and how to support small and medium-sized companies in europe. here is the place and here is the added value of the european budget and here is the perspective we should also seek for the european budget in the discussions over 2013. in order to properly shape the budget for 2013 we should take into account the logic of the multiannual perspective. it is a very well known logic. everything is moving late but moving at cruising speed at the end of the financial perspective and we should remember, as mentioned by the rapporteur, the lesson of 2011. another important lesson is the full implementation of commitments and payments, but also more than 100% consumption and implementation in many areas, for example competitiveness and innovation – 135% implementation; lifelong learning – 107%; social fund – 111% of what was assumed for 2011. there is also the lesson of reimbursements. bills for reimbursement came late in december. the inability of the commission to pay what it should pay for legitimate projects in several countries is also affected by the crisis. we are not able, due to the shortage of money, to repay rome over eur 2 billion, to repay madrid more than eur 2 billion and to repay more than eur 1 billion to athens. this is an important lesson for drawing up our draft budget for 2013 and i think for the conciliation procedure of 2013. there is also inflexibility over financial regulation; that is the inability to transfer what is underspent to what should be spent at the end of the year. these are the reasons for the cash-flow problem today and it cannot be repeated next year with the accumulation of all sorts of problems. therefore in 2013 we should be equally sensitive to negative priorities, that is what is under-implemented, but also how to boost the growth opportunities and investment opportunities for the younger generation via existing means at our disposal. additionally we have to find a place for iter financing and we also have to accommodate croatia joining as member state number 28 as from july 2013. therefore, concerning the area of savings and to prove that we are really taking into account all sorts of things in the environment of today’s europe, we must consider administration. that is why we should not grow in administration. in the commission we are starting the programme of annual cuts, not waiting for the next financial perspective but starting for 2013 – 1% cuts in the administration of the commission every year. let us hope that this time we are drawing on the lessons of experience and i count very much upon the wisdom of the people elected by the people, here in parliament.
mr president, commissioner, more and more people in europe think that this is the problem, but the real problem is this europe of austerity, sanctions and impositions, with which many of us here today do not agree. i say this because, in the debate on policy guidelines, the important thing is not to go into the details of the policies we are going to finance, but to agree on our strategy, which is where i think we are failing. i really hope that, in your words, the 2013 budget proposal is in line with what you have said here, because then we will be on the right track. but so far you have given priority to short-term and short-term debates over long-term and structural debates, you have been more concerned with the consequences of the crisis than with its causes and you have imposed austerity as the only way out of the crisis. and, as you have said, history has shown that austerity has never worked. in this report we therefore ask them to use the budget to implement measures that strengthen solidarity and stimulate sustainable economic growth. the european budget is clearly too small to get us out of this crisis, but it can and must play a decisive role in setting our priorities by putting 150 billion euros at its disposal. on 30 january, the members of the european council issued a declaration stressing the need to invest in growth and job creation, particularly in smes and among young people. they announced loudly in the commission that we were going to invest 82 billion euros in this, but the truth is that we have not heard much of that announcement since. we've gone from headline to silence. they have to work in the eu budget to develop the europe 2020 policies - which we always forget - to foster competitiveness and innovation; they have to present a budget that supports smes and prevents them from reducing their investments because of the crisis; they have to commit to a sustainable industrial policy; they have to urgently address unemployment and the rising level of poverty in the eu; and they can only do this with a serious and responsible budget, coordinated with national budgets and geared towards meeting the priorities of the union. but if you continue to look at the budget as a box full of figures to cut, you will be wrong. if you think that to finance iter we have to cut back on innovation and research, you are wrong once again. and if you continue to focus your debates on how to cut or delay payments, you will no longer only be wrong, but you will be breaking the legislation that you yourself have passed. commissioner lewandowski, we know that times are difficult, but we also know - and you have said it here today, and i hope you will keep your word - that things can be done differently and can be done better. so let's join forces, mobilize resources and meet our goals.

the following is the report by godelieve quisthoudt-rowohl, on behalf of the committee on international trade, on the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending council regulation (ec) no 617/2009 opening an autonomous tariff quota for imports of high-quality beef (com (2011) 0384 c7-0170/2011 2011/0169 cod)) (a7-0025/2012).
mr president, commissioner, this is the first time that parliament has participated in this type of procedure under the lisbon treaty, on an equal footing with the council, to give its consent to the amendment of a regulation which is, as the rapporteur said, a well-planned commitment. this regulation resolves a conflict which, as the previous speakers have said, has been going on for many years. the european union banned the import of hormone-treated meat. the united states and canada responded to the european union by raising tariffs on some products considered sensitive. these were products such as chocolate, bread, pork and juices, with consequences for large areas, in particular in my country, in the levant. on the one hand, this agreement is good news for european consumers. the european union is maintaining its position of banning all imports of hormonal beef and, in return, is opening an additional quota for imports of high-quality beef. on the other hand, european producers who had been harmed by the tariff increase benefit, since this meant a tariff burden of eur 190 million for the european union seven million, specifically, for my country. the aim is also to increase market shares for these products in the united states and canada, where exports have fallen by 90% in ten years. the european commission should therefore be congratulated for these negotiations, which prevented the united states from applying the 'cruise' measure in 2009, which would have led to an increase in the number of products to which higher tariffs would have been applied. in conclusion, we support this commitment by the european union, which ensures the protection of the european consumer and also helps us to normalize trade relations with the united states and canada. this type of negotiation can be a good example of conflict resolution. we have discussed the import of beef from the united states. spongiform encephalopathy has been around for a long time, and we're out of the woods. we must therefore ensure that long-standing and unresolved problems are solved by such agreements.

the following item is added to the agenda of the debate on the statements by the council and the commission on the 2011 progress report on iceland (2011/2884 ((rsp)).
mr president, the talk of enlargement is encouraging. no member state wants to leave the union; on the contrary, several want to join, including iceland. i welcome your desire for integration and the good pace of the accession negotiations. i say accession because that is what it is all about, accession, acceptance of the union acquis. the negotiations aim to establish the adaptations that the acceding country must make to the acquis and the timetable for doing so. the commission, in its report of october 2011, tells us that there are still no changes in icelandic fisheries legislation and that it is not in line with the union acquis. the existing restrictions on foreign investment in fisheries are also not in line with the acquis: they violate fundamental principles such as the right of establishment and the free movement of capital and services. iceland is an important fishing country, as is my country, spain, and my autonomous community, galicia. the integration of iceland will strengthen the fisheries sector in the union, but iceland, mr president, cannot remain outside the law of the union in this sector. i ask the commission to give this matter its full attention.
in writing. − in favour. the commission recognises that the sustained financial and economic crisis is increasing the pressure on national financial resources. in this context, it considers ensuring the smooth implementation of cohesion programmes to be of particular importance as a tool for injecting funds into the economy. nonetheless, the liquidity problems resulting from budget constraints are making it difficult to implement the programmes, particularly in the member states which have been most affected by the crisis. in order to ensure that these member states continue the implementation of the european fisheries fund (eff) programmes on the ground and disburse funds to projects, the commission proposal contains provisions that would allow increased payments to be made to these countries for the period they are under the support mechanisms. more specifically, it is proposed that a top-up of ten percentage points will be applied to the co-financing rates applicable to the priority axis of the programmes for newly certified expenditure submitted during the period in question. in applying the top-up, the co-financing rate of the programme cannot exceed by more than 10 percentage points the maximum ceilings set in article 53(3) of the eff regulation (75% and 50% respectively for eligible and non-eligible regions under the convergence objective).
in writing. - the economic crisis and budgetary constraints affect the implementation of the european fisheries fund, in particular in the member states with macroeconomic adjustment programmes: hungary, romania, latvia, portugal, greece and ireland. the third report on the implementation of the eff (2009) notes that austerity measures have reduced national co-financing and that the credit restriction has affected private beneficiaries, affecting the ability to access and use funds and compromising the cohesion objectives. i support the amendment of regulation (ec) no 1198/2006 so that, during the period in which support mechanisms exist, the commission can cope with an increase in payments to the countries concerned. for expenditure certified again and submitted during this period, a supplement of 10 points is proposed to the funding rates applicable to the priority axis of the programmes, without implying an increase in the total financial allocation. the new cofinancing conditions for the convergence regions and the rest, 15% and 40% respectively, may still be an obstacle to mobilisation. whether they should be reduced further will have to be considered. in addition, the possibilities of the eff itself should be reoriented and the financial instrument of regulation (ec) no 861/2006 should be included.

in writing. − in favour. this text urges states which have yet to ratify the un convention on the rights of the child or ilo conventions nos 138 and 182 to ratify and implement these conventions swiftly; expresses the view, moreover, that states should implement all appropriate policies to foster awareness of child abuse in the labour market and of the need to comply with existing national and international rules; and strongly condemns the use of child labour on cocoa plantations.
in writing. − in favour. the 2010 international cocoa agreement will replace the existing 2001 agreement, to which the eu is a party. the new agreement’s objectives are to promote international cooperation in the world cocoa economy; to provide an appropriate framework for discussion on all cocoa matters among governments and with the private sector; to contribute to the strengthening of the national cocoa economies of member countries; to strive to obtain fair prices leading to equitable economic returns for both producers and consumers; to promote an economically, socially and environmentally sustainable cocoa economy; to promote transparency in the world cocoa economy through the collection, analysis and dissemination of relevant statistics and the undertaking of appropriate studies; to strive to eliminate trade barriers; to promote and to encourage the consumption of chocolate and cocoa-based products; to encourage members to enhance cocoa quality. overall, the agreement aims to bring more transparency and sustainability into a sector on which 50 million livelihoods depend throughout the world. the international cocoa organisation (icco), established in 1973 and located in london, uk, will administer the provisions and supervise the operation of this agreement. all parties to the agreement are members of the icco.

president-in-office of the council, on behalf of the vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy. − mr president, first of all i would like to express, both on my own behalf and on behalf of the high representative, my most sincere and heartfelt condolences to all the parents and families in belgium who have suffered such terrible losses in today’s tragic accident in switzerland. our thoughts are with the families and friends of the victims and with the belgian people. after that i will turn to russia. mr president, honourable members, it is a pleasure to be here again today to discuss with you the outcome of the presidential elections in russia on behalf of high representative/vice-president ashton. let me first of all thank parliament for the strong voice it has consistently given to european citizens’ concerns about democracy, fair elections and human rights in russia. russia is our largest neighbour; it is an important business partner and a strategic partner on many global and regional issues. so it matters to our citizens what the situation is with regard to human rights and the rule of law in russia. parliament followed both the russian state duma elections on 4 december and the presidential elections on 4 march very closely. it has adopted several resolutions expressing the expectations of european citizens that russia will live up to her international commitments to ensure free and fair elections. you have also given high representative/vice president ashton several opportunities to address the plenary on these crucial issues. in addition, several hearings, organised by the committee on foreign affairs, the subcommittee on human rights, the eu-russia parliamentary cooperation committee and individual political groups, have taken place since december on these elections and on human rights more generally. catherine ashton has asked me to thank parliament for all this important work. she also asked me in particular to convey the message that she shares parliament’s concerns about the case of the arrest and death in pre-trial detention of lawyer sergey magnitsky. restrictive measures are a sensitive instrument that should be considered in specific situations and in accordance with the respective eu guidelines. the european external action service is currently looking into possible ways to convey our expectation that the investigation of this case will be taken forward properly. the russian presidential election went largely as expected. osce and council of europe observers gave a clear evaluation: opportunities were not equal during the preparations, and procedural violence occurred during the voting and counting process itself. we agree with their preliminary report and will remind russia of its international commitment to free and fair elections. high representative/vice president catherine ashton issued a statement the day after the elections with five main elements. she recognised the clear victory of vladimir putin, noted international observers’ recognition of the significant civic engagement in these elections, referred to international observers’ findings of irregularities, encouraged russia to address these shortcomings and looked forward to working with the incoming president and new government on our shared modernisation agenda, which should cover both economic and political reforms. the day after the elections, outgoing president medvedev instructed the prosecutor general to examine the verdicts handed down to 32 convicts considered by the opposition as political prisoners, including mikhail khodorkovsky and his former business partner platon lebedev. the president has also ordered the justice ministry to prepare a report on the legal reasons for denying the registration of mikhail kasyanov’s, boris nemtsov’s and vladimir ryzhkov’s people’s freedom party. these are encouraging signals. the next step: we have a strong consensus in the eu that we must engage with russia – critically, yes, but also constructively. without russia we cannot solve the regional challenges in our common neighbourhood, in syria or iran, or most of the pressing global challenges such as climate change and the environment. this approach has been quite successful recently. with medvedev and the government led by mr putin, we have been able to build more constructive relations and to achieve results. russian wto accession is one key result that will bind this large economy into the international rules-based framework. the partnership for modernisation is another one. many projects have already been prepared and launched, including technical and regulatory modernisation as well as reforms of the judiciary and civil society involvement. we have also begun a process on common steps to be fulfilled before we could consider launching negotiations on a visa-waiver agreement. all of this will be of mutual benefit. the new civic and political awakening in russia has already led to some political reforms, with the first duma reading of bills introduced by president medvedev to liberalise political party registration rules and presidential candidates’ registrations and to reinstall direct elections of regional governors. the process is encouraging and will have consequences, especially in russia’s many regions. change may be slower than one would hope, but we should have patience. it is a good thing that both authorities and protesters want gradual evolution, not revolution. a cautious but real dialogue has begun between them, and the quality and dynamics of the political situation in russia have changed. the key issue for us now is how we can support this reform process. the bilateral initiatives just mentioned provide us with an excellent basis to build on. as cathy ashton has stated, the eu looks forward to working with the incoming russian president and the new government in full support of our shared modernisation agenda. the next major step in our strategic partnership, apart from all the ongoing regular work, will be the next eu-russia summit, due to be held in russia just before the summer. i thank you and look forward to hearing your views and to your resolution, which will be adopted tomorrow.

after the presidential elections. we are dealing with an official russia which still has a certain nostalgia for the soviet union and which is allowed to veto freedom in the un security council. a russia in which the president and the prime minister, in continuous alternation of power, take place without any shame. a russia in which elections are held that do not correspond to international standards, and a russia in which arrests of opponents occur, which takes us back to a not very glorious immediate past. but, mr president, a russia which is also a member of the council of europe, a mr president, russia is very important to the european union as a neighbouring european country and as a global player and permanent member of the united nations security council. that is why we want a very close relationship with russia to address issues of mutual interest and for global governance. but there are obstacles that hinder that close relationship. we cannot be satisfied with russia's behaviour in the syrian crisis and there are recent events, such as the duma elections in december or the presidential elections on 4 march, which have left us with a feeling of disappointment, of concern. the elections did not meet the democratic standards of a european country, a member of the council of europe and the osce. we are interested in a relationship of mutual trust with russia, but the fundamental ingredient of that relationship should be the community of democratic values, common respect for human rights, multiparty democracy and respect for the democratic opposition. the modern russia we want must be the russia of shared european values. on them we could build the intense relationship we desire.

population, a country with a high level of illiteracy, a country which is largely dependent on oil as its only source of income, a country which has problems with terrorism up north, a country which, african regions, which have had a very high economic growth in recent years. i also agree with all those who have said that it is absolutely essential for a country like nigeria, which is not a poor country, to ensure that goods are distributed more effectively for the benefit of the many and to fight corruption. they try to do that, but the people who are in charge of fighting corruption don't stay in office very long - because it's a relatively dangerous job! with these remarks, i wish you a continued good debate. we need the european parliament to keep an eye on what is happening in this country, which may end up being the third largest country in the world in terms of population within the next 40 years.
mr president, commissioner, i must begin by condemning the violence that has been taking place in nigeria in recent months. nigeria is the most populous country in africa and the one with the best prospects for economic growth and attracting foreign investment. its status as an oil-exporting country allows it to obtain enormous resources which must be used for the fundamental task of fighting on behalf of the alde group. madam president, i want to start this speech by talking about people. our first priority is to free the men and women who remain today in the hands of pirates, wherever they operate. hundreds of human beings are suffering from a crime which has serious psychological consequences and require specialised attention and recognition and support which they do not now have, because the hostages of these kidnappings are being held hostage by organised, very violent mafias operating outside the union. european and national standards must recognise this. the humanitarian aid fleets, merchant fleets and fishing fleets that are victims of piracy are also carrying out lawful, fair activities, which are covered by international law. in the case of fisheries, they observe good environmental practices and support local development. from that perspective, pirates cannot justify their attacks, and we must not allow that. that is why it is necessary to extend operation atalanta, and i ask why the number of troops at your disposal has been reduced and how do you assess the somali authorization to attack pirate bases on the coast? i would like you to answer these two questions, commissioner. and what does encourage many to become pirates is poverty. today, more than 3,500 such criminals operate in organized gangs in the indian ocean alone. piracy forces shipowners, maritime professionals and public administrations to add about €5 billion to the cost of their operations each year. adding a small part of that amount to what we already spend on development and cooperation will benefit all of us, because we can eliminate poverty. in 2011, only 13% of the 237 attacks were successful, compared to 27% of those that reached their target in 2010. but the ransom payments have been record breaking. let's bet on insisting on those performances before it's too late.

madam president, commissioner, we all know that piracy on the high seas is a continuing and growing threat to human life, security and development, and is a breeding ground for violence and political instability in somalia and the horn of africa. in figures, piracy in the gulf of aden has in the last year resulted in more than a dozen deaths in 30 attacks, 200 pirates captured, almost 200 hostages; a situation which has an unprecedented impact on humanitarian aid for some six million people who need assistance because of drought and famine in the region; a humanitarian crisis which has already resulted in the deaths of thousands of people. the money shipping companies are spending on security is 40 times the amount of eu aid to somalia. while we cannot underestimate the global effort that is being made through operations like atalanta and the nato deployments, we need more efforts, more commitments, efforts that must necessarily include an anti-piracy strategy driven and supported by the leaders of central and east africa. the fight against piracy has become a global problem that requires a joint and decisive response, with a series of effective actions to tackle also the root causes of this phenomenon: youth unemployment, famines, droughts and political instability. we cannot ignore the fact that, according to the united nations, 40% of the profits from piracy in somalia have been used to finance local employment and have been invested in infrastructure for the most deprived. finally, i ask the commission and the council to continue to take decisive action to tackle the root of the problem. helping the horn of africa to end piracy, which is not only increasing but also becoming more violent, must remain our priority.

mr president, among the many issues raised by this debate i would like to highlight the issue of the emission allowance market, a market which was born with defects, to be sure. but today, the limitation of rights and the economic crisis have meant a drastic reduction in the price of carbon, that is, it is so low that it is cheap to pollute. it is therefore urgent to reform the design of a policy on this market because its deterioration threatens all green efforts, the whole green policy of the european union. if the emission allowances are not valued, the incentive to increase emissions is being given, polluting industries will not invest in new techniques and, what is worse, the financing of important projects, such as energy efficiency projects or carbon storage plants, will be jeopardised. this is the risk. it is up to us - the commission and parliament - to prevent this.
mr president, madam commissioner, i will deal with just two points and very quickly. the first is perhaps the most debated issue in the report and the one which causes the most disagreement, namely whether or not to deal with the emissions trading mechanism. obviously, like any other market 'in quotes' is suffering and is suffering downwards, but intervening in that market i think is a mistake. intervening to try to improve prices, as in other sectors, would be a serious mistake. what needs to happen is more growth. what we need to do is push it so that we can get out of the crisis and so the emissions market will be back to what it was. secondly, in relation to this road map which, as has been said here, has so many uncertainties, if we were to draw a plan with different avenues that would lead us to the final objective - which would be to have a low-carbon economy - there is one avenue, there is one route, which is the main one, which is that of energy efficiency. in that field, you can say and predict a lot of things. we have reached agreement on the energy efficiency directive with a great deal of effort from all the groups in this parliament. it is the same agreement that i and my group would certainly like to see reflected in the vote that will take place today on the report we are debating. i think, frankly, it's worth it. we have done that with energy efficiency, why don't we do that today with this report?
mr president, there is a problem that concerns me, and that is that for many people water is a non-renewable resource. water is partly renewable, not always. many aquifers are not renewable, but the water returns to the land. the problem is that it does not always return to the same place from which it came, that is to say, the water that evaporates in the mediterranean is precisely the water that rains on austria or prague, and this must be taken into account. i think that the agreements on transboundary waters are very good - and i think that the commission should put much more emphasis on this. as the directive states, a river must be managed in a uniform and unique way, but it must be much stronger and more powerful, and relations in the field of transboundary waters must be strengthened at international level. that seems to me essential, and we shall see that in the case of turkey, which will never want that, but we must insist. i think, however, that the control of the aquifers is very weak. there are technologies to control aquifers. most of the corruption is in the illegal extraction of water from aquifers. i therefore think it is essential that this point be taken into account, and there are technologies for this. i also believe that the relationship between agriculture and water needs to be reviewed, because there cannot be products that consume a lot of water and are treated as those that do not. if we put a price on water - i am a supporter of this in agriculture, and in my country it is paid, in my region it is paid - we must take into account that maize and lettuce, for example, consume much more water; then we are exporting water to all the countries to which maize or lettuce is exported. and that should be reflected in agricultural prices. it's a matter for reflection.
mr president, i come from the land of a thousand rivers, where our national poet, rosalía de castro, sang in her most famous poem about rivers and fountains. as elsewhere in europe, water has been commodified and privatized in recent years. large water infrastructure, which was not needed, was built, when citizens pay a high price to consume water and even the water from dams is not good for consumption. in this context of crisis, it is necessary to adopt a new model of water culture, to change the paradigm, to focus on sustainability. water is not just a factor of production, it is a right, an ecosocial factor, a public good. it's life for life. the two keys to the new water culture are: first, conserving and protecting water quality, preserving the functionality of rivers, streams, wetlands, and ensuring quality water resources; second, efficiency, moving to a management model... on company law, on the information society and the media, on the judiciary and fundamental rights and on justice, freedom and security. we have also agreed to work on bringing the relevant turkish developments regarding the acquis. and we will of course involve stakeholders, as appropriate, at further stages of the process. work continues also in other areas of the positive agenda. as regards ridiculed or pushed into self-censorship, but valued for their contribution to the democratic fabric of society. in the words of voltaire: we can disapprove of what someone says, but we need to defend mr president, the european social model we boast about is not only based on our pension, education and health systems, but also on a way of understanding the balance between employer and employee within companies. the labour reform that the spanish government has approved, without dialogue and without consensus, breaks with that social model and takes us away from the objectives of the europe 2020 strategy, both in terms of job creation and the quality of employment. labour reform alone does not create jobs; economic growth does. what a labour law does is define the conditions under which workers enter enter enterprises, under which conditions they stay in enterprises and under which conditions they leave enterprises. and with this reform, thanks to which 80% of workers will be unprotected because they will not be subject to collective agreements, workers may be dismissed because of a decrease in the income of companies or their hours may be unilaterally changed, what is clear is that workers will enter the labour market with more precariousness, stay in it with more fear and leave it with less compensation. that is why this reform, which is an attack on the european social model and which is committed to the competitiveness of the spanish economy only in relation to the conditions of workers, deserves a general strike like the one called for tomorrow in spain in defence of this social model.

in writing. − the eu citizenship report 2010 outlines concrete measures that the commission is taking to ensure that eu citizens are able to exercise their rights to the full in eu member states. it includes 25 of the most important obstacles that our citizens face while exercising their rights in their country of residence or across borders and puts forward solutions for overcoming them. more than 300 relevant petitions received were analysed. issues related to free movement account for approximately 25 % of the total number of petitions received. freedom of movement is one of the fundamental rights of eu citizens recognised under the treaties. the report also summarises that the greatest obstacles to exercising active union citizenship are a lack of awareness by individuals of their rights as eu citizens and a lack of clearly structured, widely publicised information explaining their rights. for all these reason, i will vote in favour of this report as it is our duty to improve this situation, which is crucial for our eu citizens.

annan’s six-point plan. together with our eu representatives at the un security council, to whom i pay tribute for their work and for their engagement, and all our member states, we have spared no and the provision of humanitarian assistance to all areas affected by the fighting must be ensured. only through a credible and sustained halt to violence will kofi annan be able to develop a parties to comply with his plan. given the government’s responsibility and record of broken promises and unfulfilled commitments, this resolution is an opportunity for the regime to change course and kofi annan in his efforts and ensure that a fully-fledged observation mission in syria is operationalised without delay. china and russia must continue to play a key role in bringing a solution to the conflict, using all their influence to ensure the security council resolution is fully implemented. i have, on a number of occasions, personally expressed my support to special envoy annan and told cooperation with the league of arab states, we have already helped build the league of arab states situation room to improve communications, and we are training them to develop their analysis and ability to respond to crisis situations. last week i convened the crisis platform again to bring together all the services of the eeas and the commission, under the chairmanship of secretary-general pierre vimont. we are putting all our instruments together, coordinating closely with kristalina georgieva and her work and humanitarian aid and support, and reaching out to all the countries neighbouring syria, both through ambassadors in brussels and through the authorities on the ground. we are working closely with all the member states to try and ensure an effective and coordinated eu response. we have suspended all types of cooperation, including bilateral cooperation, and syria’s participation in regional programmes. the european investment bank, with which we work closely, has suspended all its loan operations and technical assistance to syria. we have nevertheless maintained aid that benefits the syrian population, students, human rights defenders and the opposition. those 29 million in humanitarian aid to syria and the neighbouring countries affected. support to the neighbouring countries is also essential. i discussed these issues when i was in turkey over the weekend weekend. i remain in close contact with him and his services for whatever is needed. we are also working closely with jordan and lebanon and are ready to mobilise our instruments to respond to their requests. i have started to discuss the details of that support with the foreign minister of jordan. it is important that we continue to act as fast as we can, liaising closely with local ministries. groups, which is a critical issue in which i believe the european parliament has an important role to play. i thank parliament for its efforts in reaching out to opposition groups. our main objective the first item on the agenda is the report by mr milan cabrnoch, on behalf of the committee on employment and social affairs, on the amendment of regulation (ec) no 883/2004 on the coordination of social security systems and of regulation (ec) no 987/2009 laying down detailed rules for the application of regulation (ec) no 883/2004 (com (2010) 0794 - c7-0005/2011 - 2010/0380 (cod)) (a7-0043/2012).
member of the commission. − mr president, the regulations that are the subject of today’s discussions lay down some specific measures for the coordination of national social security systems. they make practical arrangements to protect the social security benefits of eu citizens who move across borders. these practical arrangements can only be effective if they reflect changes in the legal and social situation. since the modernised social security coordination regulations were applied in 2010, we have discovered that changes in national legislation and in working practices create a need for clarification of the text and for some small gaps to be closed. the proposal which the parliament is discussing today takes account of recent developments and concepts which were not developed in detail in the regulations. even though the proposal is technical in nature, it has a direct, practical impact on people who rely on the measures adopted at european level when they make use of the right to free movement. as this house’s recent resolution on the 2010 european citizens’ report made clear, the right to freedom of movement and residence needs to be accompanied by specific measures to give substance to this fundamental freedom. this holds true in particular for the two most sensitive issues in the proposal: the introduction of the home base principle for air crew members, and the provision for unemployment benefits for unemployed self-employed persons who return to their state of residence in which no insurance system exists. i can assure you that the compromise reached on these technical issues is in line with the spirit of the regulation, which coordinates and seeks to protect workers’ rights. it clarifies the rights of citizens and it assists institutions when they apply these legal texts. mr cabrnoch’s report makes the importance of adopting the file at first reading and approving the outcome of last year’s negotiations very clear, and i am grateful to him for keeping the compromise in mind when the amendments were drafted. the commission fully supports the amendments and wishes to thank the rapporteur for helping to foster sound cooperation between our institutions on this matter.
i should like to begin by congratulating the commissioner, the commission services and the council, and my colleague, mr cabrnoch, on the excellent work which has enabled us to find a way out of the debate on this updating of the regulation and to be able to do so at first reading and therefore to have the benefits immediately available. i would like to remind you, as other members have already said, that this is an annual exercise and that this time there are two important developments: the new article 65, which grants unemployment benefits to crossborder workers, whereas they did not have them until now, and we will review this in two years' time, even to improve it; and, above all, the new reference in article 11 to the 'base' criterion, which gives legal certainty to aircrew and clearly indicates the applicable legislation, with the concept of 'base' (home) as the basis, something which already exists in the regulation. i would like to take this opportunity in the last few seconds to say and remind colleagues and the public that, at a time when europe is so often put on the spot, we have today a clear example of how europe can benefit and improve the lives of millions of workers who, thanks to these systems of social security coordination, reach retirement age or unemployment, perfectly covered by cooperation between european states, and because there is a european union and because there is a european social model, a european social model which, contrary to what someone in the council has said, is alive and must be improved every day, because that is what people are asking for and that is what we are demonstrating in this parliament today that it is possible to do.
member of the commission. − mr president, i believe the proposal discussed today builds on the existing legislation with a view to guaranteeing eu citizens an entitlement to social security benefits when they move between member states. cross-border mobility indeed raises questions, and we have to find practical answers and solutions in a constructive atmosphere of this kind. i believe the various references to other dossiers such as, for example, the posting of workers, were also relevant and very helpful, and i listened very carefully to what was said about the impact of social housing and homelessness, because this is also an important aspect of our work in the fight against poverty. but the proposal that was discussed today makes provision for technical arrangements for effective social security coordination and does only what is necessary to make effective coordination a reality for citizens in their day-to-day lives. the commission welcomes the agreement between the council and parliament and looks forward to the adoption of the proposal at first reading.

in writing. − in favour. the outermost regions of the european union comprise a set of regions which, due to the specific characteristics associated with their physical and structural conditions and resulting from their remoteness, insular locations, difficult topography and climate, constitute a specific group of regions recognised by article 349 of the tfeu(1). these regions possess a special status enshrined in the treaty, which permits a derogation from the rules of the treaty and the adjustment of these rules to the outermost regions, by virtue of their particular characteristics and conditions. as these regions’ constraints and difficulties are permanent and distinguish them from other european regions, the eu rules and programmes cannot be applied in the same way as in the rest of the eu territory. their implementation has to be guided by a territorial approach.
