in writing. − in favour. salmon in the baltic sea are doing poorly, for many reasons. salmon is not entirely a competence of the eu, since its spawning areas are the rivers and streams of the ms, but several eu management measures exist - total allowable catches for sea fishing, minimum landing sizes, closed seasons, etc. there is also a ban on the use of driftnets to catch salmon. the com has proposed an eu-wide management plan, which by and large we welcomed. both in envi (carl schlyter opinion) and in fish we tried to strengthen the proposal, by phasing out fishing on the sea, introducing a larger minimum landing size for both salmon and trout (to prevent mis-reporting), increasing the objectives for natural spawning of salmon in wild rivers, etc. a number of our main proposals were accepted (more in envi than in fish, of course) but we lost on the phasing out of fishing on the sea itself and the common minimum landing size for salmon and trout. we were successful in improving the scope of the plan to include recreational fishing, a major part of the fishing mortality that until now has not been regulated (at eu level).
in writing. − in favour. greens support the unity of the political forces of parliament, vis-à-vis the reluctance of council to live up to the lisbon treaty. we had differences with regard to the omnibus-i, relating to the procedures for anti-dumping cases that we wanted to be better controlled by parliament. this made us to abstain in the final vote on omnibus-i. regarding omnibus-ii, we are somewhat unhappy with the treatment of gsp as mostly in the reign of implementing acts. however, given the need to send a clear sign to council that we want them to finally deal with the issue, greens should vote in favour of the omnibus-ii report of parliament.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it represents a step forward in the european union's strategy for the conservation of fishery resources. the report seeks to amend the previous regulations to include new marine regions which were not included in the previous regulations, by defining very specifically the protection areas and their species. the report extends the pursuit of fishing for fish below the size specified as suitable for not harming the reproduction of the species. this report includes a number of amendments on the authorisation of fishing techniques for different species, authorising those gear which do not endanger juvenile marine organisms and do not deplete stocks. i voted in favour of this report because it introduces technical improvements which will allow greater conservation of europe's fisheries resources.
in writing. − against the report. technical measures are the detailed regulations concerning fishing activities, such things as mesh sizes in the nets, the minimum size of fish that can be brought ashore, closed areas and seasons where fishing is prohibited, etc. most of them are collected in a few regulations limited to technical measures, but for historical reasons related to the lisbon treaty, there is a series of technical measures in a separate regulation that is time-limited and scheduled to expire on 31 december 2012. since this series of technical measures has already been renewed twice, this time, the com has decided to incorporate them into the primary regulation on technical measures (reg. 850/1998). in its proposal, it also took the opportunity to clean up a few obsolete provisions. unfortunately, the com produced its proposal very late, requiring that both csl and the ep work very fast. in favour on postponing the vote on the legislative resolution.
in writing. - i could not vote in favour of this report despite the fact that it contains important measures for the conservation of the shark population because it is causing losses in the fisheries sector. it is very important to conserve species such as sharks through sustainable fishing practices that make it possible for fishermen to avoid environmental excesses. but the fisheries sector has been facing a serious crisis for many years, with the result that the small-scale fishermen are at risk of disappearing in many member states. the obligations which this regulation will impose will lead to even greater losses in this sector, and the risk of the disappearance of this activity will be increased, since only large vessels will be able to carry the entire animal, while small vessels will not be able to meet this obligation. although it contains a number of good practices to ensure the survival of various shark species, i did not vote in favour because of the impact on small fishermen and therefore on the communities linked to fishing.
in writing. − in favour of the amended proposal (which is not the original defended by the rapporteur). an unequivocal eu ban on the odious and wasteful practise of shark finning will finally become reality after today's vote. meps have voted to prohibit the removal of shark's fins on board, making it mandatory to land sharks with the fins naturally attached. this will allow the eu ban to finally be implemented without exceptions. despite eu legislation on shark finning existing since 2003, loopholes enabled this barbaric and wasteful practise to continue. thankfully, a majority of meps has voted for an outright ban, and rejected attempts to preserve these loopholes. " every year millions of sharks are caught, their fins hacked off and the bodies simply discarded to meet the demand for shark fin soup in asia. this is not only a senseless waste, it also puts pressure on threatened shark species. banning shark finning in european fisheries is an important step but the eu should also advocate for the practise to be outlawed at international level.
in writing. - i am in favour of effective control to ensure compliance with the ban on finning practices (fining and discarding of the rest of the body) in sharks. i share the general agreement on landing fins and bodies in the same port. however, i do not think it is justified that the fins should be landed on the bodies. the latter option, rejected at the recent meeting of the iccat, entails unnecessary additional costs in the storage, handling, processing and early marketing of catches, which may jeopardise the viability of a significant segment of the sector. i support and advocate control at the port of landing through independent certification, based on parameters adopted by official institutions. a reasonable solution, and one that the industry has embraced. it would set a valuable precedent for the global control of fishing activities. only if it didn't give the expected results, he would have to resort to a more burdensome formula. i am also pleased to note that the ferreira reports on small-scale and artisanal fishing and the lövin reports on the external dimension of the common fisheries policy, both in the field of the reform of the cfp, contain many of the amendments i had tabled.
in writing. - this is a very sensitive vote because of the nature of the matter and the way the discussions in the committee on fisheries have developed. i voted in favour of the european commission's proposal because i am absolutely against the culling and therefore in favour of the full exploitation of the shark. i have supported the exception provided for in article 4 because i consider it to be an appropriate solution in the current circumstances of the sector in the iberian peninsula. the exception could be maintained for a while. it would also be desirable for the industry to carry out a thorough study of the overall costs involved. in any case, all this must be supplemented by an effective system of controls in ports of the fisheries actually carried out, and we must conform to international recommendations.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution because i believe, correctly, that the council has no power to block the commission's decision on this matter. the 1980 hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction is the law on international child abduction. the commission is concerned that all member states comply with the treaty, so that they do not refuse accession to any new state, as provided for in the convention. the council is preventing the normal development of decisions taken in this respect, whereby the commission is trying to ensure compliance with the law in force and is trying to prevent any state from refusing to accept accession. the council also refuses to consult parliament to make progress on the matter because of legal disagreements. that is why i voted in favour of this resolution.
in writing. − in favour. the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction is of great importance, as it establishes a system allowing participating states to cooperate in order to find a solution to international child abductions, by determining which courts are competent and which law is applicable when deciding where the child should reside. the convention thus provides for the speedy return of abducted children to their proper country of residence. the convention only applies between countries which have ratified or acceded to it. whereas the accession of new states must be accepted by those states which are already members in order for the convention to apply between them. the acceptance of accessions is therefore of the utmost importance.
in writing. - i voted in favour of this resolution because i think it rightly points out that there are risks to the guarantee of fundamental freedoms. in this resolution, parliament called on the council and the commission to ensure that any amendments to the international telecommunications regulation are compatible with eu law, ensuring that the internet is a free and neutral space where human rights and fundamental freedoms are respected, in particular the freedom of expression and assembly. considers that neither the international telecommunications union nor any centralised institution can be adequate bodies to exercise the role of internet regulatory authority, and regrets the lack of transparency and inclusiveness of the world conference on international telecommunications (wct-2012) of the international telecommunications union. this report has expressed concern about the decisions that various private actors gathered at this conference intend to unilaterally regulate internet freedom and impose its conditions on citizens. i have therefore voted in favour of the resolution.
in writing. − in favour. we call on the council and the commission to ensure that any changes to the international telecommunication regulations are compatible with the eu acquis and further the union’s objective of, and interest in, advancing the internet as a truly public place, where human rights and fundamental freedoms, particularly freedom of expression and assembly, are respected and the observance of free market principles, net neutrality and entrepreneurship are ensured. we also regret the lack of transparency and inclusiveness surrounding the negotiations for wcit-12, given that the outcomes of this meeting could substantially affect the public interest.
in writing. - i voted in favour of the resolution because it reflects the extreme importance of the matter and the consequent concern of parliament. climate change, which was denied by a large number of members of parliament a few years ago, must now be one of the main items on the political agenda of the international community in order to mitigate the disastrous effects that such change can produce. the resolution stresses the role of the european parliament in the forthcoming doha negotiations, insisting that parliament must give its consent to agreements reached with third countries or international organisations. the resolution calls for the eu to continue to play a leading role in reducing emissions in order to mitigate climate change. that is why i voted in favour of the resolution.
in writing. − in favour. un framework convention on climate change (unfccc) 18th session of the conference of the parties (cop-18) and the eight meeting of parties of the kyoto protocol (mop-8) will be held in doha, qatar 26.11.-7.12.2012. the doha meeting is expected to make progress on the durban platform of action, setting work programme towards agreeing a ‘protocol, legal instrument or agreed outcome with legal force under the convention, applicable to all parties’ at the latest by 2015. the mop should also adopt the formal amendments to establish a second commitment period under kyoto protocol. the envi adopted resolution is mainly a positive one, it calls for/stresses, inter alia: new protocol to ensure mitigation action in line with below 2°c carbon budget, means for the required climate action in developing countries, and robust compliance and clarity and agreement on comparability of effort for non-kp developed parties.?
in writing. - i could not vote in favour of this report because i do not share the political agenda which the european union demands of the candidate countries in its enlargement. the report contains very positive aspects, such as the inclusion, for the first time, of the fulfilment of various social aspects for countries wishing to become candidate countries. the report says that the candidate countries will have to comply with the rules of the various treaties in force in europe on social and labour issues, as well as the eu's charter of fundamental rights, in order to avoid any form of 'social dumping'. but on the other hand, this report still contains a certain political ambiguity which may cause problems for the admission of some states. in particular, as regards the peaceful settlement of disputes, the invasion of territory cannot be considered a 'dispute' and therefore the case of cyprus and turkey would raise the lack of jurisdiction of the european union. that is why i did not support the report.
in writing. − in favour. in accordance with article 49 teu, any european state which respects and remains committed to the promotion of the values of human dignity, freedom, democracy, equality, the rule of law and respect for human rights, including the rights of persons belonging to minorities, may apply to become a member of the union; whereas these values are the foundation of the european union itself and guide its action on the international scene, and must be respected and upheld by all member states. enlargement has been part of the eu agenda since as early as the 1960s; whereas since the first enlargement in 1973, the eu has grown gradually, its membership rising from the six founding members to the current 27 (soon to be 28); whereas a number of other countries aspire to eu membership, as a guarantee for a secure, democratic and prosperous future.

in writing. - this report is a step forward in the european union's strategy for militarisation. the report seeks to advance the implementation of the common security policy by taking an important step towards the eu playing a military role in the world to defend stability or human rights. the report also seeks to promote the use of cooperation funds for military purposes, arguing that there can be no development without stability, and to extend civil-military cooperation to security and defence policy. this report does not seek other avenues for negotiation and peaceful resolution of conflicts, but only extends the military route as the union's response to possible world conflicts, linking military spending to the credibility of international politics. i therefore regard this report as a real boost to the eu's strategy of militarization and have therefore voted against it.
in writing. − abstention. we tabled amendments contesting the following issues: strategic autonomy, defence budgets, need for more military action, extension of atalanta,eutm somalia, military action in north mali and alternatives, eu border control mission in libya, procurement of drones, european buying act for arms, defence research, eu budget and defence agency, military and civilian chains of command and hq. almost none of them were adopted.
in writing. - i voted against this report because it represents a step forward in the european union's strategy of militarization. the report is based on an analysis of the implications of the mutual defence and solidarity clauses. the text suggests that an attack by turkey on cyprus could lead to a clash between the defence obligations of eu countries and those of nato countries. these analyses of both clauses include unarmed attacks, such as cyber-attacks, or even intervention in the event of internal unrest that threatened a government. the report aims to extend the military powers of nato and the eu member states themselves. the escalation of military powers can only increase the risks to the european civilian population; only through demilitarisation can we guarantee greater security for the european population. i therefore regard this report as a real boost to the eu's strategy of militarization and have therefore voted against it.
in writing. − abstention. in general we supported the idea of a report addressing the issue of these two clauses. the problem with the rapporteur and also the epp group was that they have no clear objectives and strategies. as a result, the report is extremely vague and ambiguous. for greens there were two issues which were particularly problematic: 1) in our view there is a misunderstanding regarding the existing structures and capabilities of csdp. the rapporteur, supported by epp and alde argued that csdp can be one instrument for the implementing both clauses. and (2) more problematic is the link to nato and the vagueness regarding european military capabilities. the report does not clarify how nato art. 5 and the mutual assistance/defence clause should be linked or not linked politically and militarily. in our view we cannot (mis-)use the eu assistance clause for (indirectly) integrating countries like ireland, austria, sweden etc into nato and its nuclear weapons arrangements. in addition, the vagueness regarding european military capabilities is unacceptable because it does not include or exclude integrating french and british nuclear weapons into the implementation toolbox for both clauses.
in writing. - this report is a step forward in the european union's strategy for militarisation. the report seeks to advance the implementation of the common security policy by taking an important step towards the eu playing a military role in the field of information technologies and the internet. the report also seeks to boost civil-military cooperation for security and defence policy in the field of cybersecurity and calls on member states to increase their research expenditure in this field. the report does not seek to find other avenues for negotiation and peaceful conflict resolution, but only to extend the military route to the internet as the union's response to possible conflicts related to cybersecurity. the report also calls for funds for international cooperation to be linked to compliance with cybersecurity clauses, and for increased cooperation with nato. i therefore consider that the report is an attempt to promote the eu's strategy of militarization and have therefore voted against it.

in writing. - i voted against this report because it represents a step forward in the european union's strategy of militarization. the report is based on the sound assumption that the effects of climate change may exacerbate existing conflicts. but the solution to these conflicts cannot be an escalation of the arms race that increases the capacity to kill to infinity. the report also proposes european budget funds for military purposes, closer cooperation between nato and the european union, the inclusion of military elements in climate change policy, as well as its integration with energy policy. i therefore regard the report as a real boost to the eu's strategy of militarization and have therefore voted against it.

in writing. - i voted in favour of this report because it involves a commitment to an activity capable of exploiting fishery resources in a socially and environmentally sustainable way. the reform of the common fisheries policy has completely ignored the reality of small-scale and artisanal fishing and has focused on the large fishing companies which cause the greatest environmental damage to the seas. the report makes a number of proposals to support and promote these traditional fishing gear which are closely linked to the socioeconomic fabric of many european territories and their communities. the report proposes the creation of specific support mechanisms for this activity within the framework of the common fisheries policy, which is essential to ensure the survival of this activity and the sustainability of the areas traditionally used for fishing in europe. i voted in favour of this report because of the need to defend traditional fishing.

in writing. − in favour. the eu fleets fish far beyond the waters of the eu and imports fish from far and wide, so the cfp must cover those activities. the com published a communication on the external dimension of the cfp as part of its reform package and the greens were given this report. the external dimension is a vast subject and the com treated only two aspects - bilateral fisheries agreements and international fisheries management organisations. we added the aspects of foreign investment, banking, illegal fishing, joint ventures, trade, flags of non-compliance, and many others. since the basic regulation of the cfp has provisions on the external dimension, we used the report as a means of getting political support to include strong legal provisions in the cfp reform. the draft report was well received in general with favourable comments on the principles. as often happens, though, our specific proposals were less enthusiastically received and generated 284 amendments, many of them trying to weaken or negate the thrust of the report.

author. − mr president, the human rights situation in iran is constantly deteriorating. numerous cases of ill-treatment, torture, medical neglect and death in iranian prisons have been documented. sattar beheshti, a 35-year-old blogger, was arrested on 30 october by iran’s cyber police in a raid on his mother’s home in robat karim. they also confiscated a number of his personal belongings, including his computers. mr beheshti’s family tried to get information from security and judicial officials about his whereabouts and the reason for his arrest. no answer was given until 6 november, when police officials told the family that the blogger had died in custody. the authorities did not provide any explanation for his death. this is why in this resolution we strongly want to demand an immediate investigation into the circumstances of sattar beheshti’s death in custody and call for the prosecution of the officials responsible. we also have to recognise the right of the family to clarify all the circumstances surrounding his death. we also need to remember the execution, on 22 october, of ten iranians accused of drug-related offences. we are concerned that they did not receive a fair trial and they were subjected to torture during their detention. probably, in many cases, none of this is new. the problem is that we are being forced once again to ask the iranian authorities to ensure that prisoners are not subjected to any torture or other ill-treatment and that they are allowed to have regular access to lawyers of their choice and medical treatment when needed. let us not forget that iran has also ratified the international covenant on civil and political rights.
the rapporteur. - mr president, i am sorry that the commission is not present in this debate. with regard to the association agreement between the european union and central america which we are discussing today and which the house will vote on tomorrow, i would like to say first of all that this is the first agreement of this kind that the european union has concluded with a regional bloc: we have not been able, mr president, to conclude any agreement of this kind with either mercosur or the andean community, as we shall see in the debate we are going to have on the agreement concluded with colombia and peru. i also believe, mr president, that at the same time this agreement allows the countries of central america to play in the first division of the agreements which the european union has with third countries. i would also like to say, mr president, that these agreements have a threefold nature: firstly... mr president, i would ask you to suspend the sitting until there is a little more order in the chamber.
the rapporteur. - mr president, i hope the commissioner will be able to attend the debate.
the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. as i said earlier, mr president, this association agreement between the european union and central america has, in my view, two fundamental features: firstly, it is the first agreement of this kind that the european union concludes with a regional bloc, and secondly, it is an agreement that places the countries of central america in the first division of the agreements that the european union has with third countries. the association agreements, mr president, ladies and gentlemen, as we know, have three aspects. firstly, a political dialogue; in this case, the european union supported the efforts made at the san josé political-ministerial dialogue, which, thanks to a remarkable mobilization of central american political talent, was able to pacify an isthmus that went through very dramatic and very difficult circumstances. and i am pleased to note, mr president, that the european union has shown its readiness to contribute to the dividends of peace, understanding, harmony and reconciliation in that region. this association agreement now allows us, mr president, on the basis of common values and the democratic clause, to continue and deepen this path of dialogue and to try not only to maintain this dialogue in a bilateral context, but also to proceed with the extension of the bilateral agenda, turning it into a global agenda, to take account of the challenges that are arising today on a planetary scale. on the commercial side, this is a fourth generation agreement which aims to promote a progressive and reciprocal liberalisation of trade, which will create important opportunities for the citizens of the european union and central america, will offer products from this region great advantages, as they will have access to the eu market on preferential and very favourable terms - a market with great consumer power despite the crisis - and will consolidate and improve the existing facilities within the system of generalised preferences. and a side of cooperation and development aid, where the european union shows that it is not a selfish europe and that it remains the main donor of development aid, by contributing to the resolution of the problems that still remain in the region in relation to social cohesion, democratic institutions, security, respect for the environment, support for infrastructure, education, etc. i would not like to end my speech, mr president, without mentioning two subjects which i consider important. firstly, this ratification process has exposed major shortcomings in the eu decision-making process: the negotiations for the conclusion of this agreement were concluded in may 2010 and only after more than two and a half years will this house, by virtue of the powers conferred on it by the lisbon treaty, be able to speak. i believe, mr president, that this delay is undermining the credibility of the european union and, more seriously, is cutting off important opportunities, not only for the union but also for our partners, at a particularly difficult time such as the one we are living through with the crisis. i therefore believe, mr president, that we should give it some serious thought and try to improve the procedure in future. secondly, i just wanted to say that i just got back from panama. it is a country which the world economic forum has just placed among the forty largest economies in the world, it is the country with the lowest unemployment rate in the region and it is an economy which, with the enlargement of the transoceanic canal, has become a very important logistical, commercial and investment platform. it is therefore urgent that the european union should open a delegation in this country. finally, mr president, i thank the alternate rapporteurs of the committee on foreign affairs for their contribution, as well as the rapporteurs of the other committees, and i hope that, with the same majority as that adopted in the committee on foreign affairs, the house will ratify this agreement tomorrow, which will bring important benefits to the european union and to the countries of central america.
on behalf of the ppe group mr president, the european union and latin america are natural allies, with ties anchored in a great convergence of history, culture and also values. the association agreement with central america is the union's first regional agreement and i believe it is a clear support for the process of integration in central america and latin america in general. as already mentioned, the agreement is based on three pillars: political dialogue, trade and cooperation. as regards political dialogue, i believe that the agreement is in line with the european union's support for central american peace, democracy and the defence of fundamental rights, which began in the 1980s; on trade, i welcome the achievement of a predictable framework of legal certainty and the progressive expansion of the exchange of goods and services, thanks to the creation of a wide free trade area; and in the field of cooperation, the agreement will be a valuable support for the efforts needed to promote social cohesion and sustainable development. mr president, latin america - and also central america - has been undergoing a process of development and transformation in recent years, which has left behind the long period known as the lost decade. furthermore, globalisation requires all of us to coordinate better to deal with global and international challenges and threats. and in this new environment, the agreement will make our relationship with central america deeper and more effective. in addition to bilateral issues, we will be able to tackle global issues, we will deepen economic and trade matters, far surpassing the unilateral system of generalized preferences, and social cohesion will occupy an important place in our cooperation, as the central american reality demands. and one last consideration: i welcome the incorporation of panama into the agreement. we are thus strengthening central american integration by including, as mr salafranca has said, one of the most dynamic economies in the region today. and to be consistent with that - as mr salafranca has also said - the union should open a delegation in panama, where we now have only a simple cooperation office.
on behalf of the s&d group. mr president, i would like to express the support of the socialist and democratic group and my staff for the ratification of this agreement, which, as has been said, has cost a lot of work, a lot of time, but which is an important piece in the framework of agreements that will constitute a strategic relationship between the european union and latin america. we already have agreements with mexico and chile. the agreement with colombia and peru will also be discussed today and will be put to the vote tomorrow. we now look at central america, a region which we supported - as has already been said - in times of war and constant violence, and in which the european union's collaboration and support were essential for peace and democratization. only one black spot: this parliament never condemned - i do so here, modestly - the coup d'état in honduras two years ago. but in general there is broad agreement among the majority groups in this house in favour of this trade agreement, political dialogue and cooperation, which will be mutually beneficial for both parties and which also has a component - although it has been said no - of guaranteeing human rights, environmental guarantees and other aspects which will also enrich the relationship between the european union and central america. central america may seem a small region, and it is, but it is a key region in latin america, because it is a group of countries whose stability, whose democracy and whose peace are of the utmost interest to us. we should continue with the mercosur agreement, the most difficult, the most comprehensive, but we are there. mercosur, now extended to bolivia, ecuador and, before, venezuela, is already a very big pie in all aspects of the word tarta. we must not fail to consider negotiation, commissioner, which is important, urgent and necessary to bring that agreement to a swift conclusion.
opinion of the committee on international trade and development - madam president, commissioner, my first words are to congratulate the rapporteur, mr salafranca, on the great work he has done. as the opinion writer for the agreement on the committee on international trade, it has been an honor to work with you, mr. salafranca. i firmly believe that one of the fundamental pillars for overcoming this deep crisis we are experiencing is the internationalisation of our economy and our companies. this agreement will undoubtedly facilitate that primary objective. in addition to being a good agreement for the european union, i firmly believe, also, that it is a great agreement for central america. it is a good agreement because it will help the regional integration of the countries it covers. it will also be key to improving social cohesion in central america and fundamental to the economic diversification of its producing sectors. i have had the opportunity to visit several of these countries and have witnessed the enthusiasm this agreement is generating in the region. besides, one of my last visits was to panama. and in it - and here i also join the rapporteur and mr mon, i have seen and witnessed the great demand for the european union to open a delegation there. i therefore ask the commission to please reconsider the possibility of opening a delegation of the european union in panama city. finally, i would also like to acknowledge the work done by the trade commissioner, mr de gucht, and congratulate him because without his cooperation and work, this agreement would not be possible today. i hope therefore that we can celebrate the approval of this agreement tomorrow.
member of the commission. − madam president, let me just go into a couple of questions that have been put to me, in which the association agreement has been criticised. i happen to be in good company with mr leichtfried, because i have also come to the conclusion that a number of remarks have been made in this debate that go exactly contrary to the text of the agreement. you can of course have different opinions on the use of a trade agreement and i am open for such a discussion; obviously my analysis and those of the gue/ngl group and even the greens will not necessarily be exactly the same. but having been a lawyer for 25 years i have always appreciated that, when you defend a case before the court you should stick to your dossier, you should stick to the facts in the dossier, you should not plead against the dossier as has been done this evening by a number of members such as ms grèze and ms zuber. it has been said here that there was no mention – for example with respect to indigenous rights – of the international labour organization convention 169 concerning indigenous and tribal peoples in independent countries. and yet this is explicitly in the agreement. i could give you a number of other examples in this respect. the same goes for money-laundering. incidentally we should differentiate between the agreement between central america and the european union, which is an association agreement, and the agreement with colombia and peru, which is a trade agreement. but both of those agreements – and i will come back to this if need be in the next debate – contain provisions just like those in the one with south korea, i.e. with a developed economy, that promote effective and transparent regulation notably ‘to ensure that international standards for regulation and supervision in the financial services sector and for the fight against money-laundering and the financing of terrorism are implemented and applied in its territory’. it has also been said during this debate that there is no sanction mechanism in this association agreement. again that is not right because the agreement provides for recourse to appropriate measures in case any of the parties has failed to fulfil an obligation under the agreement and this can as a last resort result in the suspension of the agreement. so i personally think this is a very balanced agreement. by the way, it is not so easy to balance an agreement between a highly developed economy such as ours and developing economies, as is the case for most of the central american countries, though not all of them – there are two economies that are already rather well developed. similarly, making a region-to-region agreement with a region that is not homogenous is not easy either, but i am very pleased that we managed to have a region-to-region agreement because i believe that especially for these kinds of regions, made up of multiple rather small states, it is very important that we have a region-to-region agreement so that it can also foster regional integration. so having said all this, i really recommend to the parliament to vote in favour of this agreement. yes it will – i hope it does – boost our trade, and we need some trade in europe, especially at this moment in time. for example in 2011 trade contributed 0.6% to our growth. if we had not had trade in 2011 we would have been in a recession in 2012. so i hope it will also help our economy but i am very much convinced that, because of its balanced nature, it will also help those economies develop. i agree with all those who say that we should have those two aims: we should of course work to the benefit of our own people; we should also make sure that our counterparts take as much profit from the agreement as we do.
the rapporteur. - madam president, as the commissioner has said, there are some clarifications that are necessary. how is it possible for a member of the green group to come in and say that the agreement does not contain a democratic clause and for another member of the green group to come in and say that the agreement does contain a democratic clause, but that the clause is not binding? the democratic clause is an essential element of this agreement. how can it be said that asymmetries are not taken into account when the different degrees of tariff disarmament are clearly manifest and cater for different degrees of development? there are some members in this house, madam president, who have the bad habit of telling our partners and friends what they have to do, but central american societies, despite what they may think, are mature enough to know what is good for them and what is not good for them, and they will express themselves through their democratic parliaments. and they don't want handouts, they don't want unilateral concessions, they want bilateral agreements. this agreement really represents an extraordinary opportunity and i therefore hope that, as has happened in the proceedings in the various committees, this parliament will vote in favour of it by a majority.

the next item is the debate on the recommendation for second reading by the committee on international trade on the council's position at first reading with a view to the adoption of a regulation of the european parliament and of the council laying down transitional provisions on bilateral investment agreements between member states and third countries (11917/1/2012 c7-0328/2012 2010/0197 (cod)) (rapporteur: mr vital moreira) (a7-0389/2012).
member of the commission. − mr president, on behalf of the commission, i would like to convey our deep appreciation of the excellent cooperation with parliament in achieving a satisfactory compromise on the proposed bilateral investment treaties regulation. an intensive succession of trialogues has demonstrated that the ordinary legislative procedure allows a rich and constructive dialogue, resulting in strong and high-quality legislation. i would like to thank the members of the committee on international trade and its chair, professor moreira, for their engagement on this topic. the reason for tabling this proposal in the first place is that the lisbon treaty modernised eu common commercial policy. in particular, it transferred foreign direct investment to european level and entrusted the eu with a major additional policy tool. all the institutions agreed from an early stage that a new eu investment policy had to be based on existing experience in member states. indeed their investment agreements concluded over the last 60 years with further states constitute a precious acquis. at the same time it was, and still is, necessary to build a genuine eu policy. this regulation, as professor moreira rightly stated, is a key piece of legislation in the trade area, although not an easy one. the trialogues demonstrated that the matters covered by the regulation involved very complex legal and institutional aspects. the finalisation of the legislative process for this regulation in an early second reading would be a remarkable achievement for all of us. the regulation ensures legal certainty for european investors. they will be able to continue benefiting from the 1 400 bilateral investment agreements currently in force, as these agreements will receive a strong legal footing under eu law. these agreements will remain in force until they are replaced by union agreements. at the same time the regulation contains all the appropriate safeguards to ensure that these bilateral investment agreements will not create any serious obstacles to the smooth implementation of eu investment policy, which is a key priority. the adoption by parliament of the regulation will allow the union and its institutions to focus on the implementation of eu investment policy, by advancing eu-wide investment negotiations to ensure a very high level of protection for all european investors on a level playing field and in full consistency with the union’s wider trade and external policy objectives. i therefore call upon the european parliament to endorse the final agreement on the regulation establishing transitional arrangements for bilateral investment agreements of member states today. it is encouraging to note almost unanimous support of the international trade committee in its recent vote.
on behalf of the s&d group. mr president, commissioner, as the rapporteur said, this is very important: the rules of the game laid down by the lisbon treaty for the forthcoming bilateral trade agreements; the european union will be responsible for legislating or for providing the criteria for the states to legislate. this is a balanced regulation, safe for the states, which harmonizes this area at the level of the european union. it has been difficult because the states have resisted interference in their own decisions because of the often delicate situations caused by bilateral agreements. but the specific objective is that the european union should make progress in investment matters and therefore there must be legal certainty in relation to investment. with this report we have found the key to guaranteeing and protecting the agreements of the member states with third countries, harmonizing the investments of the european union as a whole and ensuring compliance with the decisions of the arbitration procedures - which is also important - and we must accept them. the financial responsibility must also be sought in future agreements. this regulation has brought transparency, equality, and has made it clear that agreements are not abusive and that there are no breaches.
member of the commission. − mr president, let me just briefly react to a couple of remarks which have been made during this debate – a debate which demonstrated, i believe, that there is general support for the proposal we have been making and which, through the negotiations in the trialogue under the chairmanship of professor moreira, has resulted in the text which has now been submitted to you. there was a question by mrs oomen-ruijten asking whether there will be the same high level of protection as is found now in a number of bilateral investment treaties? yes of course; i believe that the prime aim of what we have to do in the future is to make sure that every member state receives exactly the same high level of protection as is now only reserved for a couple of countries. that is what you see when you look at the 1 400 treaties: you can see that there are a number of countries that are extremely well protected and in many cases this also has to do with the size of that member state. now what i see as the commission’s duty is to make sure that every member state, even the smallest one, receives exactly the same high level of protection as is now reserved only for a couple of countries. secondly, is this going to create a kind of eternal system? i do not believe so and let me give you two answers. first, we have been asking for a number of mandates to negotiate investment treaties with singapore, with canada and with india, and we have had no problem obtaining them from the council – after discussion of course, as is right and proper. but they have entrusted to us to negotiate this on behalf of the european union. now regarding the phasing-out: will it be an eternal system? no, precisely because member states are going to insist more and more that these bilateral investment treaties become european investment treaties, because that is how they will get the same protection. so it is the member states themselves who are going to insist that we make europe-wide agreements out of the existing bilateral investment treaties. that, i think, is the logic which lies in this regulation and that is also why the commission has agreed to walk away from its initial proposal of limiting the phasing-out to a certain number of years. it was not realistic; member states did not like it at all so it was not possible to have a regulation on that basis. but having thought this over, i believe it is much more likely that the dynamic will be of the member states wanting to have the same kind of protection that will bring us to a system – it will take some years of course – which is identical for all member states, and that is what i believe the commission should be aiming at.
it is very gratifying for the members, for the president and, i am sure, for the rapporteur to meet a commissioner who knows what he is talking about and who does not come here merely to read a paper that has been prepared for him. i think that is something that we all appreciate and it is important that you are aware of the esteem we deserve for the fact that whoever is speaking to us really has a very deep knowledge of the subject we are discussing. it forces us all to be better.
the debate is closed. the vote will take place tomorrow at 12 noon.

reason that the commission has conceived of the european patent convention as something immovable, consisting in the exclusion of the court of justice - which, incidentally, has yet to give its opinion - from the system. it also allows the creation of a unified court with three seats. in reality, the commission, the member states and parliament have given up the search for a solution within the framework of the treaties, preferring the intergovernmental option of enhanced cooperation. we therefore propose that all three reports be rejected. in the end, the council won the case, but not all of it: the kingdom of spain and the italian republic have indeed brought the matter before the court of justice. the objectives pursued by the three rapporteurs are very praiseworthy, but the path chosen is the wrong one. the complexity of the system favours large companies over small ones. in my country, in spain, and in the european union, more than 90% of enterprises are small and mediumsized. we must not forget that a patent is a monopoly of exploitation and is therefore contrary to free competition. the owner of a patent has the exclusive right to exploit and market the invention. in return, he has the obligation to disseminate his invention in detail so that it can be reproduced by third parties. it is precisely the possibility of accessing technical patent information that promotes innovation to the greatest extent, while at the same time protecting inventors. so if the system does not balance the position of the patent owner with that of the legitimately interested third party, we have not made any progress. the patent system proposed to us is fragmenting the internal market. unfortunately, we already have this enhanced cooperation, but we doubt that the 25 member states involved will finally ratify the international agreement for the creation of the unified court. the system is too complex, with multiple patent protection possibilities and different courts for dispute settlement, and it is also too expensive. the fact that there are different courts for each type of appeal is not the most appropriate in terms of legal certainty, and we believe that the good faith clause in the regulation on translation provisions will not be sufficient. companies in some countries will be able to do all the paperwork in their own language, while those in other countries will have to use a language other than their own. the languages to be used will be those of countries which already have considerable competitive advantages and which will now be spared the costs of having to disseminate their inventions in an appropriate way. in short, with the compromise which is being put to the vote today we are giving up a real patent system in the european union: we have not reached a real european vision either on languages - we shall have three - or on the court - we shall have three - or on the content and scope of patents. the foundations of the building, unfortunately, are weak. i would like to end by quoting the prestigious european max planck institute for intellectual property and competition law, which points out that the unitary patent represents a significant step backwards in terms of the quality and viability of patent law, that the opportunity to modernise the european patent protection system has been lost and that this situation can only be restored if we return to the spirit and the letter of the treaties, if we all make concessions and if no one tries to impose his will on others.
madam president, today is going to be a great day for europe, its citizens and their enterprises. after 40 years of negotiations we will have a european patent which is valid in most member states, thereby easing the path to an enhanced single market. however, spain refuses to join this great european project. i find it embarrassing that spain, for petty nationalistic reasons, wants to be out. because of this, thousands of catalan innovative enterprises will be damaged by this spanish exception. as a catalan mep coming from catalonia, which generates more than 30% of new spanish patents every year, i find this astonishing. i will support this european patent because by enhancing the single market we enhance our chances of future prosperity. the spanish government seems to be providing further rational incentives for more and more catalan citizens to ask for an independent state inside the eu. ladies and gentlemen, i am saddened to have to announce that on 24 november last 112 people died in a fire at a textile factory in dhaka, the capital of bangladesh. the absence of emergency exits, inadequate safety measures and flammable materials contributed to this misfortune. now, of course, there is growing popular discontent with this catastrophe. thousands of workers have taken to the streets in dhaka, demanding greater protection. the funeral was attended by 100,000 people and we in the european parliament cannot turn a blind eye to this tragedy. there are over 4 000 textile factories in bangladesh, many of which do not have adequate safety measures. most of its exports come here to the european union, or to the united states, often under well-known brand names. the european parliament considers it important to follow up this tragedy, the working conditions in that country, bangladesh, and to analyse implications for future trade agreements. for this reason, instead of dealing with this matter with a debate on urgent matters, as planned this week, the conference of presidents decided last thursday that parliament would hold a full debate in the january part-session, including statements from the council and the commission. on behalf of the european parliament and all of you, i express my sincere condolences to the families of the victims and wish the injured a speedy and full recovery.

in writing. − abstention. the greens have nothing against helping kyrgyzstan, which can be regarded as the most democratic country in central asia, and hence on many accounts deserves help. however, we are in principle against the extension of the mfa instrument beyond the countries participating in the european neighbourhood policy. the reason for our rejection to offer mfa beyond the enp countries is that mfa is tied to the recipient country operating a structural adjustment program of the imf. hence, the conditionalities for receiving mfa are set, and the eu only participates to the extent of 10-20% in a loan supplied by the imf. for countries outside the enp, the eu has therefore no say on how the money should be spent. this is different for mfa to countries within the enp (such as georgia for which a vote on mfa will take place at the same december 2012 plenary), given that the union’s enp policy as such has the character of a structural adjustment programme. here, additional mfa funds can have added value over and above imf payments, pegged to a rigid set of conditionalities.

in writing. − in favour. europe faces today times of big challenges. the economic crisis is severely affecting our economy, our countries, our societies, our families. we face nowadays difficult times when, perhaps more than ever, we need political reflection and debate on ideas. every crisis, every stage such as the one in which we are living today, is also an opportunity to improve, to reflect on what were the reasons that brought us to this situation, to correct the mistakes made, to evolve, and thus, to make the necessary changes. the most challenging times are therefore the best opportunities to make reforms, to invent ourselves again and, thus, evolve to a better situation. europe is rapidly moving from the industrial age to a global, networked knowledge and service-based economy. that inevitably necessitates changes not only in the economy but also in the institutions and systems that were designed for a different era. emphasising the paramount importance of the transformative power of new technologies, as well as education, skills and life-long learning, this initiative seeks to stimulate debate and focus public attention on the issues that are at the centre of a successful knowledge economy.

in writing. − in favour. since the discovery of penicillin, in the 1930s, antimicrobials have revolutionised medical and veterinary practice, leading to significant reductions in the mortality rate from a wide range of serious and often fatal bacterial infections while paving the way for innovative invasive surgeries to enter widespread use. the extraordinary medicinal progress of the antibiotic era, however, risks being undermined by the growing threat of antimicrobial resistance (amr). amr is the ability of a microbial organism to flourish and survive in the presence of an antimicrobial at a usually sufficient dosage to inhibit or kill microorganisms of the same species. as a result, antimicrobial organisms may develop a profound resistance to certain antimicrobial agents to which they are ordinarily sensitive. after eighty years of widespread use, the evolution and adaptation of disease-causing microbes has resulted in many antimicrobials losing their effectiveness. this nascent crisis is a consequence of two fundamental and related issues: the inappropriate use of antimicrobials in human and veterinary medicine, and a forty-year innovation gap in the development of novel antimicrobials due to low returns on r&d investments.

the next item is the debate on the recommendation by mrs anni podimata, on behalf of the committee on economic and monetary affairs, on the draft council decision authorising enhanced cooperation in the field of financial transaction tax (com (2012) 0631 - 2012/0298 (app)) (a7-0396/2012).
on behalf of the s&d group, i would like to congratulate the rapporteur, mrs podimata, on her report and support the draft council decision authorising enhanced cooperation in the field of the new financial transaction tax. i regret that the commission proposal for a directive from september last year, adopted in its amended form by parliament, could not find sufficient support in the council. and i appreciate the position of the member states, which in sufficient numbers have shown themselves willing to establish a common system by making use, for the first time, of the enhanced cooperation procedure in the tax field. such an initiative, respecting the competences of non-participating states and the principle of non-discrimination, is the best way to avoid further fiscal fragmentation in the internal market and will contribute to stabilising the public accounts of participating states in a fair manner, reducing speculative movements in the financial system and promoting a growth and employment agenda. the new tax should form part of the european union's own resources system, so that its revenue reduces or replaces the contributions of the participating states to the union budget. it is a valuable first step towards making the commitments on financial system contribution reached at the 2009 g20 summit in pittsburgh effective at the global level and to advance a sustainable development agenda.

opinion of the committee on transport and tourism. - mr president, mr commissioner, welcome to the house. the duration of transport is just one more parameter that affects animal welfare, since it would be pointless to limit the transport of animals to eight hours if the vehicles are not conditioned to ensure minimum density and proper ventilation and if the drivers do not have the minimum training to handle the animals properly. i think it is worth making it clear that the current european legislation on animal welfare is the most ambitious in the world. the european food safety authority's scientists say that the welfare of animals depends more on the conditions of transport than on the duration of the journey. ladies and gentlemen, to be honest, i would like to say that i found the opinion of the committee on transport and tourism more balanced, and not because i was the author. all these speeches, mr president, are very beautiful. it is a pity that behind it, sometimes - and i am not dismissing everyone - there is some part that is not true, that hides interests; interests of countries that want to export frozen food and of those who have to transport live animals. why does the rule not apply to animals which are not intended for slaughter but for fattening? mr president, interests, interests, interests, not animal sensibilities.
i am opposed to the introduction of new animal welfare rules when the existing regulation already contains provisions regulating the time of journeys according to the different animal species and in accordance with the scientific knowledge we have. it is worth recalling that the european food safety authority itself has stated that there is no scientific basis for amending the current legislation and that animal welfare depends mainly on the quality of the journey, i.e. the treatment of the animals and the condition of the vehicles. it should also be remembered that transport is already required to respect a number of essential parameters, such as minimum density, ventilation, temperature or intervals of water supply or feeding. the current rules on the transport of animals are more than sufficient to ensure the welfare of animals during transport. the problem is the degree of compliance with the regulations in force. we should concentrate on improving controls to enforce the law, rather than using this debate to introduce restrictions on the free movement of goods which will not have the same effect in all countries and which would benefit some commercial interests to the detriment of others. if it is true that animals suffer on long journeys, let us not limit journeys only to animals destined for slaughter but also to animals for fattening. why make distinctions if both animals and others are entitled to be treated with dignity? i believe that this period of economic crisis is not the best time to make proposals that are not even backed up scientifically. the european union cannot afford such trifles.
madam president, there are two proposals on the table: the commission's blueprint, which outlines an economic and monetary union with all the elements necessary to ensure its proper functioning and a detailed and plausible roadmap - a document which the delegation i represent fully endorses - and mr van rompuy's report, which has a more watered-down, less ambitious vision and which abandons important elements such as a genuine common deposit guarantee system or formulas leading to the mutualisation of debt, such as eurobonds, which are necessary for an efficient economic and monetary union. important agreements must emerge from this council, ladies and gentlemen. the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect. it is inexcusably necessary both to ensure financial stability and to overcome one of the major problems preventing the euro area from growing and creating jobs: the lack of access to finance for smes. the euro area financial market is a fragmented market which, in addition to funding shortages, leads to unjustified interest rate differentials between member states. there is no justification for companies which are in the same or better position than those in other member states not being able to finance themselves or having to do so at exorbitant interest rates compared to their neighbours. there are signs that the council will dare to develop the banking union. it would be the best christmas present. nor is this the time to put short-term political interests ahead of the interests of the citizens of the european union. the urgency of the situation, madam president, must make this council change something. the council cannot continue to do things as they have been done up to now: too slowly, too late and too little.

in writing. the report also calls for the establishment of a european air traffic management system (atm) for airports. the new rules allow for the optimum use of airspace and ensure that airspace users can operate on their preferred routes, while allowing maximum access to airspace and air traffic control services. the report also proposes greater transparency, so that the coordinator or facilitator of schedules to the companies must submit an annual declaration of his economic interests in order to demonstrate that he does not share interests with the entities receiving the schedules. the text could have addressed issues related to the environmental criterion, such as noise, air pollution, climate change or energy expenditure. in any event, it represents a small step forward in improving the connectivity and usefulness of regional and national airports in the european union.
in writing. − in favour. the commission published its communication on ‘capacities at airports’ com(2011)823, with the conclusion that the capacities at airports should be increased. it identified three fields of problems in this regard: ‘allocation of slots’, ‘noise-related restrictions’ and ‘groundhandling services’. so the commission proposed new legislation on these items: i.e. a recast of the ‘allocation of slots’, replacing the existing directive by a regulation, as well as replacing the existing directives on ‘noise’ and ‘groundhandling’ by regulations. see http://ec.europa.eu/transport/modes/air/airports/index_en.htm " for the ‘slots’ regulation com(2011)827 proposal, the commission’s objectives are to ensure strengthened and effectively implemented slot allocation and use, to enhance fair competition, and it therefore proposed to introduce a possibility of secondary trading in slots, to enhance the transparency of the slot allocation procedure, to increase the slot usage from 80 % (80-20) to 85 % (85-15) as well as the slot series length, and to authorise an airport charge system. greens/efa tabled amendments on the introduction of an auctioning system of slots, related to environmental criteria (noise, local air pollution, climate change and energy consumption), but they were rejected by the tran committee vote. greens/efa supported this report.
in writing. − today the european parliament gave its green light to the new regulation governing the allocation of slots at eu airports, aiming at increasing airport capacity and decreasing delays. the text provides several new elements to the existing allocation regime. firstly, a secondary trading market for slots has been introduced. this measure will allow airlines to adjust their slot portfolios according to their operational needs, while guaranteeing a proper use of the slot and enhancing the development of airport infrastructures and services. these exchanges must take place under the close supervision of airport coordinators, so that the procedure for the sale or purchase of a slot complies with the rules and with maximum transparency. to ensure the process, the coordinators’ full independence is key to strengthening the slot allocation system and its transparency. another innovative element is constituted by the provision of a more incisive and effective sanctions regime against the so-called ‘bad users’, i.e. those carriers operating air services without a corresponding slot or when the use of the slot differs significantly from the scheduling period of the slot.

mr president, welcome to our debate, mr lambrinidis. i have been asked to speak on this subject. respect for human rights and democracy is one of the hallmarks of the european union and should, of course, be a very important part of our external action. this is the subject of the donskis and tavares reports on which we shall be voting tomorrow. i would like to make a very brief general comment. we all know that human rights are universal and indivisible, but we are also aware that in today's multipolar world some emerging countries do not share our view of the paramount importance of respecting freedoms. however, we must cooperate with these important countries, for example, to tackle global challenges. in addition, our dependence on the outside world for energy, our position as the world's leading trading power and the phenomenon of globalisation all force us to interact with the rest of the world. the treaty on european union is aware of this complex situation. it recognizes the important objective of supporting democracy and human rights, but it is right, for example, in articles 3 and 21, to include other objectives: interests, security, independence, strategy. in conclusion, what we need is for the european union to pursue - and i know that this is difficult - a foreign policy which, on the basis of our values, is intelligent and effective and capable of integrating in a balanced way the various objectives, including the defence of human rights and democracy. the european parliament, which is the creator of the sakharov prize and is certainly very sensitive to respect for human rights, must cooperate within its powers.
